facts.label: Cannabis retailer licenses ever issued and still on the register
facts.source: Washington State Liquor and Cannabis Board, cannabis retailer list dated 18 August 2026
facts.verify: Sheet 'Retailers 8-18-2026', rows where Priv Desc = 'CANNABIS RETAILER'. The file also holds 82 'RETAIL CERTIFICATE HOLDER' rows, which are excluded from every count here.

facts.label: Retailer licenses with status CLOSED (PERMANENT), 59.3 percent of all retailer records
facts.source: Washington State Liquor and Cannabis Board, cannabis retailer list dated 18 August 2026
facts.verify: Count Privilege Status = 'CLOSED (PERMANENT)' among the 1,146 retailer rows: 680. Active (issued) is 462, expired 2, closed temporary 2.
facts.note: FRAMING RULE. This is cumulative across the market's life, not an annual failure rate. Washington's first adult-use sales were in 2014, so the correct sentence is 'of every retail license ever issued' or 'over the market's life'. Never write or imply that 59 percent closed in a year.

facts.label: Retailers with status ACTIVE (ISSUED)
facts.source: Washington State Liquor and Cannabis Board, cannabis retailer list dated 18 August 2026
facts.verify: Count Privilege Status = 'ACTIVE (ISSUED)' among retailer rows. Spread across 148 cities and 38 counties.

facts.value: Everett 72, Tacoma 66, Seattle 63, Olympia 61, Bellingham 60, Lynnwood 58, Vancouver 53, Spokane 51
facts.label: Share of each city's retailer licenses that are permanently closed
facts.source: Washington State Liquor and Cannabis Board, cannabis retailer list dated 18 August 2026
facts.verify: Per city, closed/(closed+active). Everett 33 closed vs 13 active. Seattle 90 closed vs 52 active. Tacoma 35 vs 18. Spokane 23 vs 22.

facts.label: Active retailers licensed through the social equity program
facts.source: Washington State Liquor and Cannabis Board, cannabis retailer list dated 18 August 2026
facts.verify: Sheet 'SE Retailers 8-18-2026': 11 rows, all Status = 'ACTIVE (ISSUED)'. Located in East Wenatchee, Kennewick, Lakewood, Malo, Moses Lake, Orting, Puyallup, Spokane, Union Gap and Vancouver.
facts.note: Small absolute number. Report it as a count and location list, not as a percentage of anything, and do not compare it to the Massachusetts equity figures: the two states run different programs and the files are not measuring the same thing.

gaps: Closure dates are not in this file, so the pace of attrition over time cannot be shown, only the cumulative total. A time series would need historical copies of the list.
Reasons for closure are not published. Report the count, never a cause.
Sales and price data: WA LCB publishes excise tax by county but it was not pulled for this page. Do not quote WA revenue figures without it.
Tax rate: WA levies a 37 percent excise tax on retail cannabis. Not yet sourced to a primary LCB or DOR page, so it is not on the page.
